data.question: What operation-specific control links can be established around 12th & Jackson before the June 2026 expansion, and which native records can resolve the responsible personnel and approvals?
data.method: Joined SPD incident 2026-25701 to the formal Downtown Activation Team instrument, police-accountability overtime/timekeeping controls, and Seattle budget reporting requirements while keeping department-level controls separate from operation-specific proof.
data.framework: Operational participation, supervisory approval, payroll authorization, accountability findings, political relationships and improper motive are separate predicates requiring separate evidence.
data.scope: Seattle Police RTCC analyst support, narcotics surveillance at 12th & Jackson, DAT coordination, overtime/timekeeping controls and the native records needed to resolve the personnel chain.
findings: SPD incident 2026-25701 states that officers were conducting a narcotics surveillance operation at 12th Avenue South and South Jackson Street on January 27, 2026.

The same SPD record states that officers asked a Real Time Crime Center analyst to help locate a known felony-warrant suspect, and that RTCC staff found the suspect and sent his picture to arrest teams as they moved in.
Executive Order 2024-02 formally establishes the Downtown Activation Team as a multi-department place-based coordination structure including SPD and covering Downtown, Chinatown-ID and Little Saigon.
The mayoral DAT release explicitly describes targeted enforcement as part of DAT operations.

Seattle Police Accountability lists active policy recommendations concerning Employee Timekeeping and Overtime Tracking and On-call premium; these are department-level controls rather than proof of a violation in the 12th & Jackson operations.

Seattle Council budget records identify a 2026 SPD overtime increase and quarterly reporting requirements on staffing, overtime and performance, creating a concrete record surface for matching operation-specific staffing and approvals.
conclusions: RTCC support is not merely a geographic or policy possibility at 12th & Jackson; it was integrated into a documented narcotics arrest operation at that location before the June expansion.
The strongest next personnel-resolution path is native incident/operation records: RTCC audit logs, tasking products, operation plans, supervisor approvals and staffing/payroll records.
Department-level overtime controls and budget appropriations cannot be attributed to a specific operation without the matching native records.
recommendations: Recover RTCC access/query/audit records for incident 2026-25701.
Recover the corresponding narcotics operation plan, briefing/tasking product, arrest-team roster and approving supervisor chain.
Join operation dates and personnel to staffing, overtime and on-call approval records and compare the resulting chain to the March-June K3/DAT deployments.
Search OPA/OIG material only against personnel and operation identifiers materially resolved by those native records, preserving exculpatory findings alongside adverse evidence.
counterarguments: An RTCC analyst assisting an arrest operation does not establish that the analyst selected the enforcement target or directed the broader policy.
A department-wide overtime or timekeeping control does not establish misuse by a particular operation or supervisor.
DAT membership and targeted-enforcement authority do not identify the police employee who approved a specific deployment.
limitations: No low-level employee was identified from video appearance alone.
No home addresses, family information or private contacts were collected.
No political contribution or affiliation was treated as evidence of improper motive without a decision-linking record.
unresolved: Who was the RTCC analyst and who supervised the analyst for incident 2026-25701?
Who authored and approved the narcotics operation and arrest-team tasking?
Which staffing, overtime or on-call records correspond to the operation?
Did the March-June K3/DAT deployments reuse the same personnel, tasking or RTCC support chain?
